Duration: 8 hours • Start: 9:00 – 9:30 AM • Languages: English and Spanish

This day offers a deep immersion in the heritage of the Zapotec civilisation and the living art of the villages surrounding Oaxaca. Begin at Monte Albán, a ceremonial city on a mountaintop that was once the cultural and political centre of the Zapotec world. Walk among temples, pyramids, ball courts and ancient tombs as your expert guide brings this breathtaking archaeological site to life with stories of cosmic alignments, sacred rituals and daily life more than 2,000 years ago.

Continue to San Antonio Arrazola, the birthplace of alebrijes — fantastical wooden creatures carved by hand and painted in vibrant colours. Meet local artisans and watch the creative process, where imagination meets ancestral traditions. End the day in San Bartolo Coyotepec, renowned for its black-clay pottery. Visit a family workshop to see how this ancient craft is shaped, polished and transformed, entirely by hand, into gleaming works of art.

Tour Highlights:

● Walk through the sacred grounds of Monte Albán, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

● Discover the rich symbolism of Zapotec art, architecture and rituals.

● Explore the whimsical world of alebrijes in the craft village of Arrazola.

● Visit San Bartolo Coyotepec to learn the secrets of black-clay pottery.

● Enjoy stories and insights from a certified bilingual guide.

● Travel in comfort, with round-trip shared transport included.

Included: Shared transport, certified bilingual guide, admission to Monte Albán, visits to craft workshops

Not included: Meals, tips, personal expenses

During your stay in Monterrico, you can choose a boat trip through the mangrove channels. The water route introduces you to the coastal forest: tangled roots are visible at the water's edge, green canopies rise above the channels, and birds can be spotted in the branches and along the banks.

This is an optional activity for a free day. The type of boat, route, guide, timing, duration and price are agreed before the trip. Sightings of particular bird and animal species depend on conditions in the wild.

During a free day in Monterrico, you can visit the sea turtle conservation centre and learn about its work protecting nests and releasing hatchlings into the ocean. Staff explain how incubation works and why it matters for baby turtles to make their own way across the beach to the water.

This visit is offered as an optional activity. The timing, programme and price are agreed in advance. Turtle releases depend on the season and hatching; the centre confirms whether a release will take place on a particular day.

The route focuses on the natural environment the reserve was established to protect. Sightings of individual animal and bird species depend on luck; a quetzal encounter is not guaranteed.
